root_motivation: Before any shelter-pet aggregation, dedup, or matching can happen, every heterogeneous source (RescueGroups JSON:API, municipal Socrata, vendor feeds) must normalize into exactly one canonical record type with explicit optional fields — so partial sources degrade cleanly instead of forcing fictional defaults, and all downstream crates speak the same vocabulary.
user_persona: A developer building the homeward shelter-pet aggregation fleet, who needs a single foundation crate to define the canonical PetRecord, LostReport, and Provenance types that every connector, dedup, embed, and match crate will import.

acceptance_criteria.description: The homeward cargo workspace exists with homeward-schema as a library crate that builds clean (cargo build) and passes cargo test.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac1.rs: cargo check + cargo test exit 0

acceptance_criteria.description: Species covers Dog and Cat; constructing a PetRecord with an unrecognized species string fails with a typed error (no silent default).
PetRecord keeps IntakeType and Availability as distinct fields, and a validator flags the contradiction Availability::Adoptable + IntakeType::Stray within a hold window.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac3.rs: validate_pet_record returns Err(StrayHoldConflict) for that combination

acceptance_criteria.description: PhotoRef stores a source URL + optional attribution and cannot hold raw image bytes (type-level: there is no bytes field).
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac4.rs: PhotoRef struct has no bytes/data field; compile-time check + roundtrip

acceptance_criteria.description: LostReport.contact is a BrokeredContactToken opaque type with no public accessor that returns a raw phone/email string; last_seen is a coarse location type with no street-address field.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac5.rs: BrokeredContactToken has no public raw() method; CoarseLocation has no street_address field

acceptance_criteria.description: Every public type round-trips through JSON serde without loss, and deserializing a record missing any optional field succeeds via serde defaults.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac6.rs: serialize then deserialize PetRecord, LostReport, Provenance; missing-optional-field test

acceptance_criteria.description: Geo coarsening rounds any provided lat/lon to the configured precision on construction; a test asserts a precise coordinate is stored only at coarse resolution.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac7.rs: ShelterLocation::new(lat=47.123456, lon=-122.654321, precision=2) stores lat=47.12, lon=-122.65

scope: Define Species, PetRecord, LostReport, SourceId, Provenance types
Implement serde (JSON) round-trip for all public types
Implement validation that flags stray-hold availability contradiction
Implement geo coarsening at configurable decimal precision
Define ChipStatus, IntakeType, Availability, AgeBucket, Sex, Size enums
Define PhotoRef (URL + optional attribution, no bytes)
Define CoarseLocation (city/county + optional coarse lat/lon, no street address)
non_goals: Network/connector code (homeward-connectors is a separate crate)
Breed vocabulary normalization beyond a stub (full vocab is a follow-on PRD)
Image fetching or storage (PhotoRef is hotlink-only by design)
Authentication or contact relay implementation (BrokeredContactToken is opaque stub)

additional.no_let_chains: MSRV 1.85 does not support let-chains; use nested if-let or match instead

five_whys_trace.q: Why do you need a homeward-schema crate before any other homeward crate?
five_whys_trace.a: Every connector, dedup, embed, and match crate imports the same canonical PetRecord. Without a shared type, each crate would invent its own, causing impedance mismatches when data flows between them.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't each connector just define its own types and convert at the boundary?
five_whys_trace.a: Dedup and matching operate across connectors — they must compare records from RescueGroups against records from Socrata. That comparison only works if both sides speak the same type, not ad-hoc maps.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must optional fields be explicit (Option<T>) rather than absent?
five_whys_trace.a: Socrata feeds have intake info but no photos; RescueGroups has photos but no stray flag. Forcing every field to be present would require fabricating values, corrupting downstream dedup decisions.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What constitutes 'within hold window' for the stray-hold guardrail?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Validation checks only the static combination: if IntakeType == Stray AND Availability == Adoptable, flag StrayHoldConflict. The actual hold duration is jurisdiction-specific and out of scope for this crate.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should geo coarsening precision be per-record or global?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Per-construction: ShelterLocation::new takes an explicit precision parameter (decimal places). Default is 2 (roughly 1.1km). The caller controls it; no global state.
